newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Straits says sees steady cashflow.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Straits says sees steady cashflow.

text.p: Copper producer Straits Resources Ltd said on Thursday it expected to maintain cashflow from its Girilambone mine, which was forecast to produce 17,000 tonnes of copper in 1997.
Chief executive Brian Rear said in a statement that put options would guarantee a minimum copper price for most of the year's production of US2,077 per tonne, or 94 US cents a pound.
Straits earlier reported a decline in net profit for calendar 1996 to A$5.30 million from A$6.93 million in 1995.
Straits said that despite lower copper prices, sales revenue rose 17 percent to A$31.3 million due to record production at the Girilambone mine in New South Wales.
Straits has a 60 percent stake in Girilambone, its sole operating mine, which produced 16,282 tonnes of copper in 1996, up 27 percent on 1995.
The other 40 percent is held by Nord Pacific Ltd.
Chief executive Brian Rear said the profit result reflected exploration acitivity and costs associated with the development of new projects.
Exploration and development expenditure almost trebled to A$12.9 million, Rear said.

Copper resources attributable to Straits more than doubled to 700,000 tonnes, two further copper projects were brought to pre-feasibility status and the company established itself in several prospective gold properties, he said.
Rear said an average copper price of US$1.15 a pound was received in 1996, aganst an average cash operating cost of 52 cents a pound.
Total cashflow from operations rose to A$12.08 million from A$11.15 million previously.
Straits recently completed the purchase of an 80 percent interest in the Sebuku coal project in Indonesia as part of diversification plans.
Straits was down eight cents at A$2.20 at 11.40 a.m. (0040 GMT).
